meaning:
κυριεύω
(κύριος), [in LXX chiefly for מָשַׁל ;]
to be lord or master of, to rule (over): C. genitive obj., Luk.22:25, Rom.14:9, 2Co.1:24; absol., 1Ti.6:15; metaphorically, ὁ θάνατος, Rom.6:9; ἡ ἁμαρτία, Rom.6:14; ὁ νόμος, Rom.7:1 (cf. κατα-κυριεύω).†
(AS)

renderings.bsb: He might be the Lord of

elsewhere.note: He said to them, “The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who have authority over them are called ‘benefactors.’
knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more. Death no longer has dominion over him!
We don’t control your faith, but are fellow workers with you for your joy. For you stand firm in faith.
which in its own times he will show, who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings, and Lord of lords.
